reason: VVG 46a gives continuation/administration duty, Art. 81 gives step-in, notice and representative; both needed, true in DE/FR/IT.
VVG art. 1 al. 2-4: four weeks if medical exam, starts on handing over or sending, release if no acceptance; matches question in all versions.
Art. 4 VVG states disclosure duty, written/text form, definition of relevance and presumption for precise questions in all three languages.
Art. 7 DSG covers privacy by design from planning, proportionality criteria and minimal default settings; consistent in DE/FR/IT.
Art. 60(1)(a) DSG: intentional incomplete access answer by private persons punished on complaint with fine up to CHF 250,000.
Art. 27 DSG lists the media grounds (sources, drafts, opinion formation) and the personal work tool ground; all languages agree.
Art. 25(2)(g) requires recipients plus Art. 19(4) info on foreign state and safeguards; 25(6),(7) give free and 30 days; both articles needed.
Art. 36(1),(4),(6) DSG support legal-basis rule, name/address/birthdate exception on request and refusal grounds in all languages.
Art. 29 DSG allows refusal/deferral on Art. 26 grounds and requires stating the reason; matches question in DE/FR/IT.
Art. 13a UWG lets the court reverse the burden of proof for factual advertising claims when appropriate given the parties' interests.
Art. 16a UWG requires quantity, price and unit price for measurable goods, with Federal Council exemption; consistent across languages.
Art. 19 UWG gives duty, subjects and BZP refusal exception; Art. 24(1)(d) gives fine up to CHF 20,000 for intentional breach; both needed.
Art. 4a UWG makes active and passive private bribery unfair and excludes minor socially customary advantages; matches all languages.
Art. 389 ZPO: domestic award appealable to the Federal Supreme Court under BGG unless chapter provides otherwise; no Art. 390 agreement made.
Art. 378 ZPO covers advance on costs, options when a party does not pay, and new arbitration or state court action after withdrawal.
Art. 185 ZPO: court puts questions, parties may comment and propose changes, court sets deadline for the report; all languages agree.
